newsitem.title: FRANCE: France calls on nationals to leave Sierra Leone.
newsitem.headline: France calls on nationals to leave Sierra Leone.

text.p: France on Wednesday urged its nationals in Sierra Leone to leave the West African state where a military coup ousted an elected government and Nigeria is pressuring the new rulers to abandon power.
"We strongly advise the French who are in that country to leave," foreign ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt told reporters.
There are about 100 French citizens in the country, nearly all of them in the capital Freetown where the coup took place.
Rummelhardt said France's embassy in nearby Guinea was in charge of evacuating French nationals from Freetown to Conakry.
He added that Paris was in contact "with our partners about the security of the French."

The United States said on Tuesday that the helicopter ship USS Kearsarge was steaming toward Sierra Leone with 1,200 Marines but no request had yet been made to evacuate Americans from the African nation.
